subs: In under two minutes, you'll know how to learn your part for the next concert.
First, type the code your choir gave you.
It brings in your programme and your scores.
Sing back a little do-re-mi pattern, one step higher each round, then lower.
That's how the app finds where your voice is comfortable.
The setup measures any delay: you just sing “ta” on each click.
Your notes scroll toward the white line, and the blue line is your voice.
Keep the blue line on the orange bars.
Those are the other voices, so you can see where you sit in the chord.
The little bubble tells you how many cents sharp or flat you are.
Every piece is cut into short sections, and each section climbs five levels.
Level 1: slow, with your part playing.
Level 3: alone against the other voices.
Level 4: no note names, only the chord to start.
Level 5: off book, from memory, on two different days.
So level 3 means I'm ready for rehearsal?
The coach tells you why: sinking on long notes, late after rests, wrong notes in bar 12.
Tap the note, and it loops just those bars, slowly.
Home shows today's plan, paced to your rehearsal and concert dates.
Ten minutes a day is plenty.
So, here's what to do right now.
1: put on headphones and tap “Start voice setup”.
2: open the first piece on Home and sing level 1 of its first section.
Tomorrow, Home shows your next step.
